string.text: Master switch. You can also toggle the tracker with F9 during a mission.
Hides the marker, distance and crosshair color while a menu (Esc, etc.) is open. Turn this off if the tracker disappears during normal play.
Show the landing prediction while a bow is wielded.
Show the landing prediction while a crossbow is wielded.
Show the landing prediction for javelins, throwing axes, throwing knives and stones. Siege engines have their own switch under Siege engines.
Show the landing prediction while you operate a ballista, catapult or trebuchet.

When a shot would hit a siege engine (ballista, catapult, trebuchet, ram or siege tower), the marker and crosshair turn light blue. Works for siege engine shots and for bows, crossbows and thrown weapons, such as a stone thrown at a battering ram.
Sphere drawn where the projectile is predicted to land.
Radius of the landing marker, in metres.
Draw the predicted flight path as a line from you to the marker.
Recolors the game's own crosshair to match the marker: white = ground, green = enemy, red = friendly, light blue = another siege engine (siege shots only).
Use ring if crosshair can't be recolored
If the game's crosshair can't be found or tinted, draw a colored ring around it instead.
How far in front of you the fallback ring and the crosshair distance text are drawn (metres).
Master switch for the distance readout.
Show the distance beside the landing spot.
Show the distance beside your crosshair.
The prediction ends on the first enemy in the path (turns green).
The prediction ends on the first ally in the path (turns red).
How much of your forward/backward speed is added to the projectile. 1 = full, 0 = none. (Sideways and vertical speed are never added, matching the game.)
Writes above the landing marker what the prediction hit: terrain, an agent, or the scene object's name and physics body flags. Use it to find objects the arrow should fly over.
